title: Заступничество Шефа и переполох на кухне  (The Chef Steps In and Chaos in the Kitchen)

segments.t: Standing up for Elena's son, Chef Barinov tells Nagiyev to punish him instead of the boy and offers to cover the dry-cleaning bill, earning Vasily's grudging respect. Meanwhile, Max's sabotage causes a tray crash in the dining room that sets Senya and Ilya at each other's throats.
Нафига ты что бы тарелку сразу брал?
Из-за тебя вон сколько блюд переделают теперь.
Ты не слышишь, я говорю, я не виноват.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Dima, he is here as my guest.' The grammar packs 'Dima' and 'invited' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'If you want to punish him, punish me instead.' Max anchors the line on 'do you want', while 'me' completes the thought.
'I can pay for your dry cleaning.' Notice how Russian expresses 'can' and 'dry cleaner’s' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'I have plenty of experience with that.' In Russian, the idea of 'by' flows naturally into 'experience' without extra filler words.
'This is my restaurant.' The grammar packs 'this' and 'restaurant' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Both of you remember that.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'remember' and finishing on 'both'. Dmitry answers right away.
'Whatever your heart desires.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'what' and 'soul' in a few short words.
'Yeah, some respectable place this is.' The meaning hinges on 'yes' working together with 'station' in spoken Russian.
'Those are not eggs.' Notice how Russian expresses 'this' and 'eggs' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
Нафига ты что бы тарелку сразу брал?
'Why on earth did you grab all those plates at once?' The grammar packs 'the heck' and 'took' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Из-за тебя вон сколько блюд переделают теперь.
'Because of you, we have to remake all these dishes now.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'because of' and 'you' in a few short words.
Ты не слышишь, я говорю, я не виноват.
'Are you deaf, I told you it was not my fault.' Max anchors the line on 'you', while 'guilty' completes the thought. Dmitry answers right away.
'Of course it was not his fault.' The grammar packs 'of course' and 'guilty' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.

Из-за тебя вон сколько блюд переделают теперь.
Ты не слышишь, я говорю, я не виноват.
